solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Add white oily solid to jug — put in with other things spun round

indicators.note: the jug is placed inside the other piece, so 'put in' signals a container
spun round means the abbreviation is turned to read backwards

parts.note: et cetera, abbreviated ETC, means 'and other things'
an amphora is a two-handled ancient jug or jar

explanation.surface: An instruction to stir a white oily substance into a jug along with other ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spun round' reverses the et cetera abbreviation to CTE; 'put in' places the ancient jar inside. 'Add ... to' makes the definition a verb, and 'jug' is not the vessel being filled.
explanation.definitionFit: Camphor is a white waxy solid, and to treat something with camphor is the verb formed from it.

clue.text: Get some wine with a holiday coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: vac is the informal short form of vacation, a holiday

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a bottle to take on a forthcoming holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: A VAC read upwards gives the answer; 'Get some' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish sparkling white wine made by the traditional method, a type of wine.

clue.text: Eat in Paris, entertaining a middle-ranking industrialist?

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: manger is the French verb 'to eat'

explanation.surface: A French-speaking host dines with a mid-level businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful definition: a manager sits in the middle of a firm's ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A person running a department in business is someone between workers and directors in rank.

clue.text: Short term? I say — that would excite one of the members of staff!

definitions.text: one of the members of staff

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A pupil's quip that a short term would thrill a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that would excite' rearranges SHORTTERMISAY into the answer, a schoolteacher of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher of the past in a school, one of the teaching staff in a common room.

clue.text: Letting children talk puts quite a few off

indicators.note: removing many letters from each end leaves a stretch of the phrase in view

explanation.surface: Allowing youngsters to chatter drives several people away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts quite a few off' strips the letters around childREN TALk.
explanation.definitionFit: A letting is the hiring out of a property, the same as a hire arrangement for payment.

clue.text: Half the competitors with an obsession about doing well

indicators.note: the obsession word goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it

indicators.note: only half of the word for competitors is kept, the second three letters dropped

parts.note: rivals are competitors

explanation.surface: A half of the field are fixated on succeeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' keeps only the first three letters of the competitors word; 'about' wraps the obsession around them. To have 'a thing about' something is an idiom for obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: Flourishing or prospering, as a successful business is.

clue.text: Ugly old woman social set cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a crowd is a social set, a group of friends

explanation.surface: An unattractive elderly lady whose circle of friends has dwindled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the D off CROWD.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal and unkind slang for a plain elderly lady, as in 'old crow'.

clue.text: Beam help to the north — speed around

indicators.note: the speed word goes around the other piece

parts.note: rate means speed

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Directions for sending a signal northward and racing around.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to the north' means reading upward, so the help word comes out as DIA; 'around' then wraps the speed word about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to shine or send out rays, as the sun does.

clue.text: Fabric gets to shrink, though, over time, ending in garbage

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means it comes first

parts.note: to wince is to shrink back in pain
yet can mean though, nevertheless

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word garbage is taken

explanation.surface: Cloth that shrinks in the wash and eventually becomes rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A brushed cotton cloth used for nightwear, a soft textile.

clue.text: So there's poison spread round a particular meat!

indicators.note: the poison is spread round the short word, enclosing it

parts.note: venin is a toxic substance found in snake venom

explanation.surface: An alarmed cry that some meat has been laced with poison.
explanation.walkthrough: Venin is a lesser-known word for animal toxin; 'spread round' opens it before its last letter to hold the short word. 'there's' is only linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer flesh, one specific kind of meat.

clue.text: Fast woman never (not ever!) going after randy man

indicators.note: the woman and the shortened word come after the randy man

parts.note: a ram is slang for a lustful man
Ada is a woman's name

indicators.note: the word ever is taken out of never, leaving a single letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman who refuses ever to chase after a lecherous man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ever' removes EVER from NEVER, leaving N.
explanation.definitionFit: The month in the Islamic calendar during which Muslims abstain from food in daylight.

clue.text: Male conviviality Jack has abandoned, calming down

indicators.note: Jack is left out, dropped from the merrymaking word

parts.note: jollification is merrymaking, festive fun
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A man quits the party mood and settles down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has abandoned' takes J out of JOLLIFICATION; M goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeasement or soothing, the act of pacifying someone's anger.

clue.text: What seems like a small area for a ball?

definitions.text: What seems like a small area for a ball?

parts.words: What seems like a small area for a ball?
parts.note: the ball is the Earth, and modern communications make the whole world feel like a small settlement

explanation.surface: A question about a cramped ground for a ball game or a small dance venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests sport or a dance, but it is the globe itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the world viewed as one community linked by communications.

clue.text: Promotes the second man and causes trouble

parts.note: raises means promotes, lifts up
in Genesis, Cain, Adam's son, is the second man to appear

explanation.surface: A boss promotes the deputy, and chaos follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to make a great fuss or create a disturbance.

clue.text: Arrangements that may come after American employee's salary review, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are said aloud

parts.note: in American English a pay rise is a raise, so the reviewed salary brings 'a raise'

explanation.surface: Plans that may follow a staff member's pay review in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans say 'raise' where Britons say 'rise' for a pay increase; 'a raise' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly displays or groupings, such as figures set out in rows and columns.

clue.text: Native in great poverty getting caught out

indicators.note: the caught letter is put out, removed

parts.note: indigence is extreme poverty
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An impoverished local resident who gets arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting caught out' removes C from INDIGENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in a place, an original inhabitant.

clue.text: Victor embraces old women — one of those people with fans?

definitions.text: one of those people with fans?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a winner is a victor

explanation.surface: A champion hugging elderly ladies, a celebrity with admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' suggests admirers, but they are the fans that blow chaff from grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who separates grain from chaff using a fan or a current of air.

clue.text: Plan to modify car noise

indicators.note: to modify is to alter, so these letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: An intention to change the sound a vehicle makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to modify' rearranges CARNOISE.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline of possible events or a projected sequence, as in planning ahead.

clue.text: A monarch to lose strength after revolution in the country

indicators.note: revolution turns everything round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
to tire is to lose strength

explanation.surface: A ruler weakening once an uprising has broken out in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: AERTIRE read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An African state on the Red Sea coast, which is a country.

clue.text: King is satisfied with what fate has dealt

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
to have met a demand is to have satisfied it

explanation.surface: A monarch accepts his destiny contentedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Destiny or fortune, the lot assigned to someone by fate.

clue.text: Great artists giving a new look to Artemis

indicators.note: a new look means the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Painters reimagining the goddess Artemis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving a new look to' rearranges ARTEMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian plural of a word for masters of an art, especially musicians.

clue.text: What David must have been against Goliath without a stone!

definitions.text: What David must have been against Goliath
definitions.meaning: set against or matched with an opponent in a contest
with the stone taken out, as of cherries or olives

explanation.surface: David faced Goliath and needed his sling stone, so being without one is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: matched in combat, and having its stone removed, like fruit.

clue.text: Seated to drink pint initially, this person's time for a double

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: sitting means seated

indicators.note: only the first letter of pint is taken

parts.note: the setter speaking: this person is = I'M
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A seated drinker downing a pint, then claiming it's time for a double measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a double' looks like a spirit measure but means a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact likeness of someone, a perfect lookalike.

clue.text: Unliked Oxford academic of great ferocity

definitions.meaning: Dr John ..., the Oxford dean in the rhyme 'I do not like thee, Dr ...'
a literary adjective meaning cruel and fierce

explanation.surface: An unpopular Oxford don known for his savage temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the disliked Dr of the rhyme, and the old adjective for savage.

clue.text: Team of flyers sounded triumphant, on song

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it follows it

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
crew is an old past tense of crow, to cry out in triumph

explanation.surface: Pilots who celebrated loudly with a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounded triumphant' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it is the old past tense of crow, to exult; 'on' puts it after the song word in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The people who staff and operate an aircraft, a flying team.

clue.text: The aforementioned pig knocked over plant

parts.note: this refers back to the thing just mentioned

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: an elt is a young sow, a dialect word for a pig

explanation.surface: The pig previously mentioned toppled a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns ELT into TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly weed with purple flowers, the emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: Adult in drama who survived when many perished

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: Noh is traditional Japanese masked drama
A is the film classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up in a play who outlived many others.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical builder of the ark escaped the Flood that drowned the rest of mankind.

clue.text: Encouraging trust in dear client when things go wrong

indicators.note: things going wrong means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Reassuring a valued customer during a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when things go wrong' rearranges DEARCLIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning giving grounds for belief or confidence, as in references.
